taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Effective Content Security Policy enforcement across headers, HTML policies and frame contexts
controls.source_trace: Resolve the policy applying to the protected document and sink. Separate Report-Only from enforcement; combine multiple enforced policies as simultaneous restrictions. Follow nonce creation and propagation into the actual inserted script.
controls.implementation_branch: If several enforced policies are present, test the intersection, not the most permissive header in isolation. Attribute the tested policy to the actual document/frame. A nonce read by privileged automation is not an attacker-readable nonce; strict-dynamic and parser-inserted versus dynamic scripts need separate consumer evidence.
controls.operational_method: Retain response headers and the position/time of each meta-delivered policy relative to the challenged resource. A meta policy does not retrospectively block earlier content and cannot express every header-delivered directive. Identify unsupported/ignored directives from the actual engine diagnostics. Compare insertion after activation with the same harmless marker before activation; only the applicable enforced policy can serve as the tested security gate.
controls.controlled_verification: In an owned fixture, compare the legitimate nonce-bearing bootstrap with one inert untrusted script marker at the same sink and capture whether execution occurs.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: An unsafe-looking directive or report-only violation is not a bypass; CSP absence alone does not establish an injection path.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Retest allowed bootstrap and rejected untrusted insertion under the repaired effective policies and the same browser context.
